Typical beam currents ranged from 10 to 20 microA.
The energy was stepped in 5- to 20-keV intervals
depending on whether the cross section was expected
to be rapidly or slowly changing based upon the
energy dependence.
The surface barrier detectors were double-
collimated with a series of slits and apertures to
only view the center interaction region of the beam
with the gas target.
The Ne gas was injected at 10 Torr of pressure and
was passed through a liquid nitrogen cold trap after
being recirculated for reinjection into the system.
For the measurement of the 20Ne(alpha,p)23Na and the
20Ne(alpha,p1)23Na reaction cross sections, 4He
beams in the q = 2+ charge state were accelerated to
energies from 3.5 to 6 MeV. The beams were then used
to bombard a natural Ne target created with the
Rhinoceros extended gas target system. Six ruggedized
100-microm-thick Si surface barrier detectors were
installed at 45, 60, 90, 105, 120, and 135 degrees to
detect charged particles emitted from induced
reactions. Data from each silicon detector were
compiled into histograms that typically contained
four to six distinct peaks. These peaks corresponded
to the various reactions that took place in the
target chamber.

To extract total reaction cross sections, the
differential center-of-mass cross-section data for
the 20Ne(alpha,p0)23Na and 20Ne(alpha,p1)23Na
reactions were fit using a weighted sum of Legendre
polynomials. From the fits, the total cross sections
could then be calculated as sigma = 4*pi*a0.
